data.name: Surajit
data.gender_notes: Surajit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who brings the sun to the earth, a god or a king. The name Surajit carries the meaning “Bringer of Light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Surajit usually hope their child will grow to embody bringer of light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Surajit belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bringer of Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Surajit total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Surajit carries a rich cultural significance in Hinduism, reminiscent of the radiant sun god, Surya. In Hindu mythology, Surajit is believed to be a king who brought the sun to the earth, illuminating and enriching people's lives. The moniker carries an aura of regal majesty and the promise of warmth and light.
data.spiritual_significance: In a deeper, spiritual context, Surajit represents the divine power that illuminates the world around us and the inner recesses of our souls. It symbolizes the spirit of positivity, enlightenment, and wisdom, shedding light on our path and offering us guidance and inspiration in our journey of personal growth and self-realization. Additionally, the name may be connected to the idea of the ultimate enlightenment or liberation from the cycle of death and rebirth, symbolized by the radiant sun.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Surajit: Receiver of Sun's Light. Embodiment of the radiant and enlightening power of the Sun God.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'सूरजित' (Sūrajit), meaning 'Conquered by the Sun'. It is believed that this name was given to children born when the sun was in a powerful position in the sky.

historical_references.reference: Surajit was a king of the Vatsa kingdom in ancient India during the 5th century BCE. He is best known for his role as a host to the Buddha during one of the Buddha's visits to the kingdom.

Surajit is also mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, where he is described as a king of the Anga kingdom. He is a contemporary of the Pandava prince Bhima and is known for his prowess in battle.
